occurrence_evidence.claim: McDonald’s and IBM tested voice ordering at more than 100 U.S. drive-through locations.
Reports described unwanted items entering live orders and unsuccessful attempts to correct them.
Reports described speech from adjacent lanes becoming confused in the order-taking workflow.
In June 2024 McDonald’s announced the IBM pilot would end; a July 26 shutdown deadline was reported separately.
McDonald’s continued to consider future voice ordering; its statement did not disclose success criteria or a finding that the test succeeded or failed.

prior_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Incorrect generated orders were used for live fulfilment, giving the order representation more assurance than its accuracy supported. Reported adjacent-lane confusion separately shows input from one customer context being bound to another order. These are bounded reported mechanisms, not findings that every pilot location failed. The reports do not establish a separately required verification step or a substitute completion condition used to declare the ordering task finished.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Customer speech was repeatedly converted into inaccurate order representations and propagated into live order fulfilment despite not meeting the interpretation accuracy required for transactional reliance, producing unwanted items, failed corrections and recurring operational errors.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: Public reports document order confusion between adjacent drive-through lanes, supporting a target-binding failure in which interpreted order material associated with one customer or lane was treated as applicable to a different customer or lane context.
